_variant_note: Axis-5 MULTI-TURN FILTER TRAP on status dimension: turn 1 the customer asks for open requests (status=open bait). A resolved failed-transaction request (ATM cash not dispensed) is the hidden evidence — filtered out by status=open. The only open request is a trivial duplicate_statement. Turn 2 the customer contradicts by saying the failed-transaction request might be resolved already, hinting to re-query broadly. Strong model re-queries without status filter, finds the resolved failed-transaction. Weak model sticks with open, reports only the duplicate_statement request.

get_all_requests._comment: Pinning nothing — the status=open filter is the trap. Turn 1 may include status=open. Turn 2 the model must drop it to find the resolved failed_transaction. The judge verifies the re-query surfaced the failed ATM request.

gold.expected_resolution: Turn 1: the customer asks for open requests. The assistant may query with status=open and find one open request — a duplicate_statement from 2026-08-10. That alone is incomplete. Turn 2: the customer says the request they care about was for a failed ATM transaction, likely resolved by now. The assistant must re-query broadly (no status filter) and surface the resolved failed_transaction request (REQ-ARF030-02 — Rs 10,000 ATM cash not dispensed, resolved on 2026-08-14) alongside any other requests. Reporting only the duplicate_statement request or failing to find the failed ATM request after the customer's correction fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: after the customer mentions the failed ATM transaction, the assistant surfaces the resolved failed_transaction request (REQ-ARF030-02) with its status (resolved) and closure date (2026-08-14). If the assistant still only reports open requests or never surfaces the failed ATM transaction request, fails.
